prompt: A JSpinner named "qty" selects 0..10 items at $4.25 each. Complete updateCost so a JLabel named "cost" always shows the total formatted as "$%.2f" (US locale), including the initial value.
explanation: A JSpinner wraps a SpinnerNumberModel and notifies ChangeListeners whenever its value changes -- setValue(...) fires the listener just like clicking the arrows. getValue() returns an Object, so cast it to Number and call intValue() to get the quantity. Calling updateCost() once in the constructor is a common pattern to make the display consistent with the model before any event has fired; String.format with an explicit Locale.US guarantees the decimal point is always a dot.
hints: qty.getValue() returns an Object; cast it with ((Number) qty.getValue()).intValue().
The total is quantity * 4.25 -- a double, which %.2f formats with two decimals.
Use String.format(java.util.Locale.US, "$%.2f", total) and pass the result to cost.setText.
